claim: WHAT WAS PATCHED (2026-07-18): the exploit was a weakly-connected-component hole in the division Jaccard. Pre-patch, a GT division counted as a TP whenever the matched predicted nodes merely shared ONE connected component that contained ANY predicted fork anywhere. The fix requires directed local topology instead.
quote: A few of you might be aware that an exploit of our metrics was found, specifically in the division Jaccard score. We have made a patch and will re-score all submissions as soon as possible (likely Monday). Submissions that did not actively exploit this will not have their scores affected.

claim: The patch commit message names the hole exactly, and the patched metrics.md spells out the new requirement: sharing a weakly connected component is no longer sufficient.
quote: updating metric to patch weakly connected component exploit  ///  Directed local topology. The parent anchor must be the predicted fork or its immediate predecessor, and the daughter matches must lie downstream of the fork on their assigned branches.

claim: THE EXPLOIT WAS THE HUB NODE, AND IT IS DEAD. The pre-patch exploit was a public notebook (outwrest/metric-hack-minimal-baseline-tta-2gpu) that post-processed only the submitted CSV: it added one synthetic hub node at t=-1000, z=y=x=-10000 joined to the roots of up to 1400 largest trees, plus a chain of 5 synthetic division events at sentinel coordinates. It was reported to the organisers on 2026-07-17, the same day as the patch commit.
quote: Adds one synthetic "hub" node at sentinel coordinates (t=-1000, z=y=x=-10000 — clearly outside any real acquisition volume/time range) connected to the roots of those trees. Appends a chain of 5 synthetic cell-division events (divider → child, continuation), also at sentinel coordinates

claim: The formula has a floor but no ceiling: adjusted_jaccard = max(0, jaccard * (1 - 0.1*(T_pred - T_true)/T_true)). T_pred below T_true multiplies the score UP, to a hard maximum of 1.1x as T_pred approaches zero. A worked example on train clip 44b6_0b24845f: edge Jaccard 0.98, node ratio -0.29, adjusted 1.0102.
quote: The max(0.0, ...) puts a floor on it, but there's no corresponding ceiling. So when a submission predicts fewer nodes than estimated_number_of_nodes, the ratio goes negative and the multiplier ends up greater than 1.

claim: T_true is NOT hidden - it is read from the GEFF metadata key estimated_number_of_nodes which ships with the data, so a submission can read its own target node count at inference time and steer T_pred to the bonus side.
quote: with N_true read from estimated_number_of_nodes in the ground truth metadata. ... a faithful prediction has fewer nodes than the estimate, the ratio goes negative, and the factor comes out above 1.

claim: COROLLARY THE FIELD IS GETTING BACKWARDS: over-detection is nearly free, so detection thresholds are probably too high across the field. The break-even line is exactly 1 - 0.1*over-prediction, so 10% more nodes needs only a 1% relative gain in edge Jaccard to pay for itself.
quote: Over-detection is almost free. A predicted node that matches no ground-truth node is never a false positive; the whole cost is the adjusted-Jaccard term. The line is exactly 1 - 0.1 x over-prediction, so 10% more nodes has to buy only a 1% relative gain in edge Jaccard to break even.

claim: But duplicate detections are pure cost: node matching is one-to-one bipartite, so a twin one voxel away matches nothing and moves edge Jaccard not at all while costing ~9% of the node budget. Naive union-ensembling of two detectors without a merge pass pays this in full.
quote: Duplicating a detection costs ~9% and buys nothing. Node matching is a one-to-one bipartite assignment, so a twin one voxel away matches nothing: edge Jaccard did not move at all, only the node count. If you take the union of two models' detections without a merge pass, you pay this in full.

claim: The patch quietly added three more submission-shaping rules to the EDGE metric that are not on the Evaluation page: edges not spanning exactly one timepoint are DROPPED (so gap-closing t+2 links contribute nothing), duplicate edges collapsing onto the same GT edge are deduplicated, and out-degree is capped at 2 by keeping the TWO LOWEST EDGE IDS - so CSV row order decides which two arcs of an over-linked node survive.
source: royerlab src/tracking_cellmot/metrics.py @ aa65e90, confirmed independently in 733877
quote: Keep the two edges with the lowest EDGE_ID per source and drop the rest with a warning.  ///  [733877] divisions now require directed local topology rather than shared weak connectivity, edges spanning more than one frame are dropped, and merged edges are collapsed.

claim: CODE-DERIVED, NOT FROM A THREAD: those three edge-metric rules are applied only inside _evaluate_matched_graph, which returns a dataframe. evaluate() then passes the RAW, unfiltered graph to evaluate_divisions(). So the division term never sees the one-timepoint filter or the out-degree cap - a fork built from arbitrary-Dt edges is still a fork to the division metric. This is the surviving structural seam worth testing locally.
quote:
edge_attrs = _evaluate_matched_graph(graph, gt_graph)
 ...
    div = evaluate_divisions(
        graph, gt_graph, scale=scale, max_distance=max_distance,
    )

claim: CODE-DERIVED: the patched TP test accepts a daughter match at the GRANDCHILD level, and pred_lineages is built as {child} union successors(child). So a second daughter arc can be routed through an intermediate node rather than attached directly to the fork. Combined with the finding above, this is the one hub-node-adjacent variant the patch does not obviously close - UNLIKE the dead version it needs REAL matched daughters, so it is a routing trick, not fabricated signal. Test it against the patched scorer before trusting it.
quote: pred_lineages = [{child, *pred_graph.successors(child)} for child in pred_graph.successors(pred_div)]

claim: CODE-DERIVED: a predicted fork is only a division FALSE POSITIVE when local GT evidence exists - the fork itself must match (within 7 um) a GT node with out-degree >= 1, or its child/grandchild branches must land in two different GT components, or its branches must be locally merged. With GT ~2.8% annotated, roughly 35 of every 36 forks are invisible to the metric, so a fork proposer needs only ~3% GLOBAL precision to break even.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS ABSOLUTE FORK COUNT, NOT PRECISION. Division FPs enter the denominator 1:1 against the ~151 GT divisions, so J_div = TP/(N_GT_div + FP). One competitor's ILP at division weight 0.5 found 1 real division alongside 3,260 false ones, giving div_j ~ 1/3260. Reaching div_j ~= 0.22 with ~40 TPs needs total FP ~= 31, i.e. a whole-corpus fork budget in the low thousands - not the ~100k an unconstrained ILP emits.
quote: For me division_jaccard never rises above 0.0004, at any weight tested. Even at 0.5, where the ILP does find 1 real division (div_tp=1), it does so alongside 3260 false ones. div_j = tp/(tp+fp+fn) ≈ 1/3260 - swamped to near-zero by the FP volume.

claim: That same post states the consequence bluntly: weight-tuning ALONE cannot produce a real division contribution - it only chooses between suppressing everything and drowning a few real forks in thousands of fake ones. Division recovery has to come from a different signal, not from a knob on the existing ILP.
quote: For me division_jaccard never rises above 0.0004, at any weight tested. Even at 0.5, where the ILP does find 1 real division (div_tp=1), it does so alongside 3260 false ones. div_j = tp/(tp+fp+fn) ~ 1/3260 - swamped to near-zero by the FP volume.

claim: CAVEAT on that 0.22: the subtraction only isolates the division term if edge_jaccard stayed constant. Parent->daughter edges also count as edges, so dropping a daughter link creates an edge FN too and the 0.022 delta splits across both terms - making 0.22 a bound rather than a value. claim: The subtraction method is nevertheless sound in principle: a fork-free submission scores adj_edge_jaccard with the division term contributing exactly zero, so one paired submission does give the split.
source: 734192 (comment by Arul Prasad S P) + royerlab metrics.py summarise()
quote: summarise() drops the division term entirely when a submission contains no divisions at all (score = edge_jaccard if not has_divisions). So a fork-free submission returns your pure adjusted edge Jaccard, and the division term follows by subtraction — one submission for an exact split.

claim: CONSENSUS IS WRONG ABOUT WHY DIVISIONS HURT. The most-cited evidence that divisions are dangerous is that -0.006 ablation. But division FPs only count in the ~2.8% annotated region, which cannot produce a loss that size. The cost is on the EDGE term: the second arc becomes an edge FP wherever its source matches an annotated GT node linked elsewhere, plus any added nodes pay the node-count penalty. Divisions should be added by RE-LINKING existing detections, never by adding nodes.
quote: A predicted edge with a source node that matches a GT node that is connected to another target node. [is an FP]  ///  [716952] division edges hurt (0.784 → 0.778)

claim: The field's own recommended ordering is detection -> linking -> division, with detector misses compounding: edge recall is approximately node recall SQUARED times conditional linking accuracy, so a detector miss costs twice.
quote: detection -> linking -> division. detection should come first, once detection is solid, it's easier to improve others.  ///  Edge recall ≈ node recall² × conditional linking accuracy. This means detector misses are especially expensive.
